The test image shows a corn leaf with:
- White/silvery bleached streaks running along the leaf length, parallel to veins
- Green tissue interspersed between the bleached areas
- Small brownish freckle-like spots scattered throughout the leaf

Top candidates: **Goss_wilt** (black freckling + water-soaked streaks), **Stewarts_wilt** (bleached leaf streaks), **Maize_streak_virus** (streak pattern). Let me view reference images.

The Maize_streak_virus shows alternating green/light stripes (lower right), and Goss_wilt (top right) shows white/bleached streaks very similar to the test image. The Stewarts_wilt reference shows young seedlings, not matching. Let me check one more candidate.

Downy mildew shows whole-plant yellowing of young plants — does not match.

**Final analysis:**

The test image shows:
- Extensive white/silver bleached streaks running parallel to leaf veins across most of the leaf
- Small brownish/dark freckle-like spots scattered throughout (the "black freckling" diagnostic of Goss's wilt)
- Irregular boundaries between green and bleached tissue
- Shiny/silvery appearance consistent with bacterial exudate

This matches **Goss_wilt** very closely:
- The Goss_wilt top-right reference panel shows nearly identical white bleached streaks with similar distribution
- The brown freckles in the test image match the diagnostic "black freckling in water-soaked lesion edges"
- The silvery appearance matches "bacterial exudate may give leaves and lesions a shiny appearance"

Maize_streak_virus shows narrower, more regular alternating green/yellow stripes (not the broad white bleaching with freckles). Stewarts_wilt references show seedling-phase symptoms. Downy_mildew doesn't match at all.
